td._comment_chain: approachChain is the berth order a train steps through on the way IN, nearest-last. It gives (a) the set of berths whose strike-in is recorded, and (b) an ordering so the CLOSED backstop can tell whether a train is still upstream of its close anchor. Derived from TD step order (see the berth-chain derivation) and verified against SMART.

schedule._comment_tiploc_station: TIPLOC of the crossing's OWN station (Portslade, CRS PLD — verified against CORPUS; note it is PSLDAWH, not PORTSLD). Used only to read whether a CIF schedule CALLS here (arrival/departure present) or merely passes, so a passenger service beyond the ~2h LDB window is classified correctly instead of defaulting to non-stopping.
schedule._comment_tiploc_approach_call: SOUTHWICK (CORPUS-verified STHWICK) sits INSIDE eastbound approach berth 0006. Services calling there spend a median 160s in 0006 (range 124-203) against 49s (44-79) for those that don't — two disjoint populations, so the 0006 strike-in means completely different things depending on the calling pattern. VALIDATED against a full day of TD: this flag reproduces the observed split with 0 mismatches in 93 runs. (Fishersgate, also on this stretch, does NOT split it — 41/93 mismatches — so do not swap it back on the assumption that the nearest station is the relevant one.) Read from the CIF schedule for every service, then applied to LDB-sourced trains by UID/headcode.

openLagSecs._comment: Anchored to TD clear-step time, NOT bestTime. Derived from 24 Jun 2026 observer session cross-checked against FOI (auto-raise on FM/AC track-circuit clear). passenger west n=6 (obs 15-23s), re-measured 31 Jul n=3 (13,15,30 -> mean 19) so 18 CONFIRMED; freight east n=2; freight west n=0 DELIBERATE GUESS.
openLagSecs._comment_east_passenger: 45 -> 35 on 2026-07-31. 45 was never a measured value: 24 Jun observed 36-43s (n=4) and 45 was adopted as a safety margin. Re-measured from the 31 Jul observer session (barrier-up minus the train's own 0002 clear-step strike): 23,31,32,32,35,43,46 -> n=7, mean 35, median 32. Corroborated independently by the prediction stamp on the same session: all four stamped opens fired EARLY (-3,-13,-14,-22s, mean -13s). Pooled over both sessions n=11 spanning 23-46s, mean ~36, so 35 is insensitive to which session you weight. The margin is deliberately GONE: it was indistinguishable from a miscalibration, and the confidence band is where uncertainty belongs. Accepted trade (Rich, 31 Jul) — about half of eastbound closures will now reopen a few seconds LATER than predicted, where at 45 almost none did. NOT split by stopping/through: this session hints at it (stopping 46,31 vs through 43,32,32,35,23, and a train accelerating from a stand plausibly takes longer to clear) but n=2 stopping is not evidence. Revisit once trainClass has been recorded for a few sessions.

closeTrigger._comment: CLOSE start = per-class berth strike-in + offset. EASTBOUND USES PER-CLASS ANCHORS because approach berth 0006 CONTAINS SOUTHWICK: services calling there sit in 0006 for ~150s, those that don't for ~50s, so one anchor cannot serve both. Measured over 7,579 eastbound runs / 77 days of TD logs (2026-07-25). Offsets = median(berth->crossing) - 140s, where 140s is the observed barrier-down lead before the crossing (24 Jun observer taps, crossing-CLOSE = 127/152/257, n=3 — THE WEAK LINK; the anchor CHOICE is robust to it, the offsets are not). Cross-check: the same arithmetic reproduces class B's independently field-calibrated +100s as +106s.
closeTrigger._comment_east_classes: stopping = calls Portslade, NOT Southwick (1H Victoria semi-fasts): 0008->xing med 189s sd 28, n=2228; anchored 0008+40 (biased ~1 IQR early, catch-every-closure over accuracy; median-unbiased would be +49). NOTE 0006 is UNUSABLE for this class — its strike lands a median 29s AFTER the barrier is already down, which was the pre-2026-07-25 bug. stoppingLocal = calls Portslade AND Southwick (1N/1S/2Y Brighton services): 0006->xing med 246s sd 58, n=4542; 0006+100 UNCHANGED (the one field-calibrated number, 24 Jun n=5 cluster 80-113s). fast = calls neither Portslade nor Southwick, passenger: 0008->xing med 158s sd 68, n=256 — WEAK, the analysis classifier was contaminated. ecs = 5xxx: 0008->xing med 226s sd 83, n=522 — WEAK. freight = 6xxx/7xxx: 0006->xing med 161s sd 55, n=31 over 5 headcodes; freight is ~100s SLOWER than fast passenger at every berth so it must NOT share their rule. Class A has ZERO barrier observations (for 1H services the barrier is already down on arrival, so the observer never logged a separate CLOSE — that selection bias is what produced the original +100s error). Field session on 1H east needed; they cross ~xx:15 and ~xx:45.
closeTrigger._comment_safetynet: safetyNetSecs.east 210 -> 145. 210 was sized against a claimed ~280s strike lead that measurement showed to be 149s, so the backstop fired BEFORE the anchor for 34/34 class-A trains — it was the primary close path, not a backstop. 145 puts it ~30s AFTER the class-A anchor (0008->bestTime min 212s observed, anchor at +185s relative) so the precise strike wins. Side effect, intended: safetyNet now < predictedLeadSecs (145 < 180), so the confirmed close is LATER than the predicted one and the frontend 'Soon' state stops being dormant. Cost on a genuinely missed strike (measured 0.093% of crossings) is CLOSED ~20-30s later. Also gated by position — see approachChain.

east._comment_confirmedMayFollowPredicted: Opt-in: allow the CLOSED gate to sit LATER than the predicted close. True only here, because safetyNetSecs(145) < predictedLeadSecs(180) is deliberate eastbound — it is what makes the frontend 'Soon' state live instead of dormant. Everywhere else the backstop is clamped to the prediction, so a pair of unrelated config values can't silently produce a window where the countdown has passed zero while the app still says CLEAR.

west._comment: BERTH-ANCHORED since 2026-08-01 (was `departure - 45s`). offsetSecs = transit[berth>XING] - 92s, where 92s is the observed close lead (crossing minus barrier-down) from n=11 westbound barrier observations (8 on 24 Jun, 3 on 31 Jul). The ANCHOR is well grounded, the OFFSET is not: over n=771 westbound crossings the berth strikes predict the crossing 2.5x better than Darwin's departure estimate (sd: 0005 19.6s, 0003 21.7s, liveDep 48.8s, schedDep 253s). 0003 chosen over 0005 despite the marginally better sd because it fires earlier and stays feasible. Deliberately NO dwell term — three measurements killed it: CIF booked dwell has only two values (30/60s) against realised 0-180s; refitting on booked gave sd 61s, WORSE than the old rule's 43s; and subtracting live dwell DOUBLED sd (13.5 -> 25.8s) because it is the difference of two minute-rounded times. Raw 0005>XING sd of 19.6s cannot contain minutes of dwell variance, so there is nothing to remove.
west._comment_lead: crossingLeadSecs is the ONE calibrated number here: the observed seconds between barrier-down and the train reaching the crossing, from n=11 westbound barrier observations. Each class's offset is DERIVED at runtime as transit[berth>XING] - crossingLeadSecs, so it follows the transit table when that is regenerated instead of drifting away from it. Only the anchor BERTH is per class, chosen so the derived offset stays positive: a rule cannot fire before the strike it is anchored to.
west._comment_prestrike: predictedDepartureLeadSecs is the PRE-STRIKE prediction, used only while TD cannot place the train at all — the westbound analogue of east predictedLeadSecs. 46s because for an LDB westbound bestTime IS the departure estimate, the crossing follows it by a measured 46s (sd 16s, n=8), and the close leads the crossing by 92s. A CIF westbound falls to crossingLeadSecs instead, because its bestTime is an interpolated CROSSING time, not a departure. Dropping this and letting closeBefore take over moved an unplaceable train's close 105s early and re-merged periods the clear-step merge key separates.

stopping._derived: 153-92 = +61s. anchor n=771 (crossing-0003 = 156s, sd 22s); lead n=11. 95.2% of westbound traffic

freight._derived: 121-92 = +29s. transit n=37; one barrier observation gives 0003+39s, within 10s. 0.5%

ecs._derived: 148-92 = +56s. transit n=266; barrier lead n=0 GUESS. 0003 would be -3s, infeasible. 3.5%

fast._derived: 94-92 = +2s. transit n=60; barrier lead n=0 GUESS, and FRAGILE — fires ~instantly on the strike, so pipeline latency eats the margin. 0003 would be -39s. 0.8%

west._comment_unknown: A train whose class cannot be resolved falls to `stopping` (see _classOf/_eastClass fallbacks), which is the right default: 95% of westbound traffic is stopping.
